headline: Phil Foden scores hattrick in Man City's 5-1 rout of AEK Athens
summary: The England playmaker marks a stunning return to form after a 10-month goal drought and mental health struggles.
details: Phil Foden scored a hattrick as Manchester City crushed AEK Athens 5-1 in the Champions League on Tuesday at the Etihad Stadium.
The 26-year-old England playmaker had struggled with mental health issues and hadn't scored for 10 months prior to a recent goal against Ipswich.
Elliot Anderson opened the scoring early in the first half, with Foden doubling the lead before the break. Rayan Cherki added a third before Foden completed his treble in the second half.
Despite the win, City's future remains uncertain as they appeal a verdict regarding over 100 breaches of Premier League financial rules, which could lead to a massive points deduction.
Even without Erling Haaland, who started on the bench due to a foot injury, City have won 10 of their 11 games in all competitions this season.
The match saw 17-year-old academy graduate Floyd Samba make an appearance, showing flashes of talent on the flanks.
caption:
A hattrick and a homecoming! Phil Foden is back in blistering form as Man City dominate AEK Athens.

Phil Foden scored a hattrick as Manchester City crushed AEK Athens 5-1 in the Champions League on Tuesday at the Etihad Stadium.

The 26-year-old England playmaker had struggled with mental health issues and hadn't scored for 10 months prior to a recent goal against Ipswich.

Elliot Anderson opened the scoring early in the first half, with Foden doubling the lead before the break. Rayan Cherki added a third before Foden completed his treble in the second half.

Despite the win, City's future remains uncertain as they appeal a verdict regarding over 100 breaches of Premier League financial rules, which could lead to a massive points deduction.

Even without Erling Haaland, who started on the bench due to a foot injury, City have won 10 of their 11 games in all competitions this season.

The match saw 17-year-old academy graduate Floyd Samba make an appearance, showing flashes of talent on the flanks.

headline_marked: 7-goal thriller: [[Liverpool beat Villarreal 4-3]] after trailing by two
headline: 7-goal thriller: Liverpool beat Villarreal 4-3 after trailing by two
summary: The Reds storm back from a 2-0 deficit at Anfield to maintain a perfect start to their Champions League campaign.
details: Liverpool overcame a two-goal deficit to secure a 4-3 victory over Villarreal in a high-scoring Champions League clash at Anfield on Tuesday.
The Spanish side took an early lead through Georges Mikautadze and Sergi Cardona, capitalizing on a rotated Liverpool squad and a defensive error by Virgil van Dijk.
Alexis Mac Allister and Ronald Araujo fought back to level the score before halftime, with 18-year-old Rio Ngumoha providing a key assist for Araujo.
Mac Allister scored his second of the night 25 minutes from time, and substitute Florian Wirtz sealed the win with a goal to complete the comeback.
With this victory, Liverpool move alongside Paris Saint-Germain at the top of the Champions League table with nine points from three games.
Villarreal, managed by Inigo Perez, struggled with defensive lapses on crosses, leaving them with only three points from their first three matches.
caption:
From 0-2 down to a 4-3 win! Liverpool pulls off a stunning comeback at Anfield.

Liverpool overcame a two-goal deficit to secure a 4-3 victory over Villarreal in a high-scoring Champions League clash at Anfield on Tuesday.

The Spanish side took an early lead through Georges Mikautadze and Sergi Cardona, capitalizing on a rotated Liverpool squad and a defensive error by Virgil van Dijk.

Alexis Mac Allister and Ronald Araujo fought back to level the score before halftime, with 18-year-old Rio Ngumoha providing a key assist for Araujo.

Mac Allister scored his second of the night 25 minutes from time, and substitute Florian Wirtz sealed the win with a goal to complete the comeback.

With this victory, Liverpool move alongside Paris Saint-Germain at the top of the Champions League table with nine points from three games.

Villarreal, managed by Inigo Perez, struggled with defensive lapses on crosses, leaving them with only three points from their first three matches.
